propositions: Escaped-defect measurement is incomplete: only 1.1% of current bugs (7/648) have provenance metadata, preventing true bug-escape rate and detection-stage efficiency calculation.
Plan-review adoption rose from 29.2% (Q2) to 79.5% (Q3) for review-before-claim, but first-pass verdict remains 49.0% with p90 attempts at 8, consuming 114.72 LLM calls per eventual PASS.

Code review first-pass rate is 97.4% (1,178/1,209), but caused_by blame attribution is demonstrably noisy and does not discriminate source-quality signals, and Gerrit reviewer independence was not measured.

Ticket closure cycle time is rapid (p50 1.52 hours, p90 0.56 days) and commit hygiene reached near-complete adoption (90% trailers, 83% DCO, 99% Change-Id in Q3), but these operational metrics do not establish sustainable quality or causality with defects.

Code structure shows forward debt risk: 35 modules at or above 720 LOC, 15 at or above 780, 4.09% duplication, and same-file retouch in 47.7% of consecutive touches, with larger diffs and initial plan non-PASS as candidate risk signals only.

Deterministic plan-review churn and escaped-defect observation gaps are prerequisite blockers; risk-tiered review, debt management, and maintainership evidence require validated prospective signals and do not yet have proven causal impact on quality or escape rate.
